gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the carry-on AC power banks cost about three times as much per watt-hour as the small stations sold beside them: $2.64/Wh for the Goal Zero Sherpa 100AC ($249.95, 94.7 Wh) and $3.51/Wh for the Omnicharge Omni 20+ ($249, 71 Wh), against $0.93/Wh for the BLUETTI Elite 10 Mini ($119, 128 Wh), $1.01/Wh for the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 ($289.99, 288 Wh) and $0.75/Wh for the Tenergy T320 ($225.99, 300 Wh), all priced on the makers' US stores on 2026-11-14.
standout_why: I opened three of the result pages. thunderboltlaptop.com lists six no-name 86-99.9 Wh AC banks with only 'Check Price on Amazon' links and no prices. geekchamp.com (cited by ChatGPT) prices Amazon no-name banks, RIVER 3, Explorer 240 v2 and Elite 30 V2, but gives no Sherpa price and no price per Wh. macworld.com (cited) lists the Elite 10 Mini at $119 with 128 Wh and 3.97 lb and says to check with the airline, but it is a station roundup with no Sherpa, Omni or mophie. So the Elite 10 Mini's $119 price is already on a cited page. Pricing the whole category per Wh, with the carry-on premium stated next to it, is on none of them. I did not open the gearlark, rottenwifi, mobilestalk, macmyths or engadget pages.
decides: This confirms the split our page already makes rather than changing the pick. Pay the about $2.64/Wh Sherpa 100AC premium only if the unit must go in carry-on. If it stays on the ground, the $119 Elite 10 Mini gives 35% more energy and twice the AC watts (200 W against 100 W) for less than half the Sherpa's price, but it is 128 Wh. That is above the usual 100 Wh limit, so Macworld says to check with the airline, and it weighs 3.97 lb by Macworld's figure. The Omni 20+ loses on price, costing the most per Wh of anything priced. Separately, our table says the Sherpa has 100 W USB-C, but Goal Zero's page lists two USB-C PD ports at 60 W each. That needs re-checking before rebuild.
